title: Because they're only little once
passage: Those first walks to the park. Tiny fingers curled around yours. Moments like these deserve the Pellora Glide, with hand-stitched trim and our signature champagne finish. You'd never give them less than your best. Don't start with their stroller. From $1,249.
cue: You'd never give them less than your best.
explanation: The ad uses tender images and parental guilt to justify a $1,249 stroller. Love for your child doesn't tell you whether champagne trim makes this stroller safer or better.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_fear: Nothing here warns of danger; the ad leans on tenderness and guilt, not fear.

passage: Did you SEE what the Fenmoor Gazette wrote about our Kestrels? After everything this team has given Kestrel Point? I've never been so proud to wear the purple. Anyone with an ounce of hometown pride knows they're the best team in the league, period. Game day Saturday, be loud!
cue: Anyone with an ounce of hometown pride knows they're the best team in the league
explanation: Ray answers a critical article with indignation and team pride. Feeling proud of the Kestrels doesn't show they're the best team in the league; standings and results would.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_pity: Ray isn't asking anyone to feel sorry for the team; he's stirring up pride and indignation.

title: Re: Saturday launch support
passage: Hi Joaquin, fair questions about whether testing could wait until Monday morning and whether Saturday counts as overtime. The client did move the launch up, so the pressure is real. But remember how this team pulled together when the Ferris account nearly walked? That's who we are. I'd hate for anyone to be the one counting hours when this team needs them. So I'm counting on all of you at 9 Saturday. Kara
cue: I'd hate for anyone to be the one counting hours when this team needs them.
explanation: Joaquin asks two practical questions, and Kara answers neither; she invokes team pride and the guilt of 'counting hours' instead. Those feelings don't show Saturday work is necessary or fairly paid.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_pity: Kara isn't asking for sympathy over her own hardship; she uses team pride and guilt to fill the weekend shift.

source: Trustee Royce Danforth · Fenmoor school board
passage: The nutrition panel says the cricket-flour cookies are high in protein, safe and cheaper than the current snack. Fine. But picture your seven-year-old biting into a cookie made of ground-up bugs. I described it to a room of parents last week and watched their faces. That reaction tells you everything about whether this belongs in our cafeterias.
cue: That reaction tells you everything about whether this belongs in our cafeterias.
explanation: Royce concedes the panel's findings, then asks the board to decide based on disgust. Parents' grimaces don't tell us whether the cookies are nutritious, safe or affordable.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_fear: Royce doesn't claim the cookies are dangerous; he relies on disgust, a different feeling, to override the evidence.

passage: You worked thirty-plus years for this. You worked the weekends, you showed up when it was hard. You deserve a retirement that feels like a reward, not a compromise. That's why the Harrowgate Legacy retirement plan is the right home for your savings. The fee schedule's in your packet, but honestly, what matters is how you want to feel.
cue: honestly, what matters is how you want to feel
explanation: The adviser stirs pride and a sense of being owed, then presents the retirement plan as the answer while waving off the fees. Feeling deserving says nothing about whether this product suits your savings.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_pity: The adviser isn't asking you to sympathize with anyone's hardship; he flatters your pride and sense of reward to make the sale.

title: Shoppers bristle as Osterbrook market goes card-only
passage: Vendors say counting cash cost them hours each week and that 94% of sales were already by card. Longtime shopper Wes Harlan wasn't swayed: 'After all the money we've spent at these stalls, this is how they treat us? Any decision that leaves loyal customers feeling this insulted is the wrong decision, simple as that.'
cue: Any decision that leaves loyal customers feeling this insulted is the wrong decision
explanation: Wes doesn't dispute the vendors' reasons; he argues the change is wrong because it makes him feel insulted. His hurt feelings are real, but they don't show going card-only is a bad decision.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_pity: Wes isn't describing a hardship to win sympathy; he treats his feeling of insult as proof that the decision is wrong.

source: Music teacher Elena Vasquez · Brookside school board
passage: When Mateo played his first solo at the spring concert, his grandmother cried in the front row. Moments like that matter, but they're not my main argument. Band costs $38 per student, the lowest of any elective, and it's the only course that fills the arts credit students need to graduate. Cutting it would save little and leave students with no way to earn that credit.
cue: Band costs $38 per student, the lowest of any elective
explanation: Elena opens with a moving story, then rests her case on cost and graduation requirements. The emotion frames the argument; the facts carry it.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_emotion: The story isn't doing the work: Elena's conclusion follows from the low cost and the arts credit, which hold however you feel.

title: Hear every word at the dinner table again
passage: Remember catching every joke at family dinners? Auralis dual-microphone aids were tested by the independent Halden Audiology Lab, where wearers understood 34% more words in noisy rooms than with standard single-mic aids. That's the difference between nodding along and joining in. Try a pair free for 45 days.
cue: where wearers understood 34% more words in noisy rooms than with standard single-mic aids
explanation: The ad uses warm family imagery, but its claim rests on an independent test of understanding speech in noise, which is exactly what dinner-table listening needs.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_emotion: The feeling matches what the evidence supports: an independent test shows better understanding in noisy rooms, the very benefit the ad describes.
